title: Add typed RAG scaffolding for Kotlin + Swift with structured-output linter and compact telemetry probes
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation: Teams building mobile-first apps requested a small, typed RAG scaffold that demonstrates how to wire Redis-like local indexes, typed tool bindings, and structured-output linting across JVM and iOS clients. This quickstart provides a minimal Kotlin SDK example and a Swift example that share a compact authoring playbook, a structured-output linter spec, and a lightweight telemetry probe harness.

What this PR adds (summary): 1) quickstarts/kotlin-swift-typed-rag/ - a new folder containing: README, Kotlin sample app (Ktor-based microservice), Swift sample (Combine-based app shim), shared authoring/playbook.yaml with scenario templates, structured-output schema and a small struct-linter config, and telemetry probes (latency + token-cost) that emit compact JSON events suitable for Redwood Console ingestion. 2) A CI smoke test workflow that builds the Kotlin sample and runs a macOS-linted Swift compile check in the matrix. 3) docs/snippets/typed-rag-mobile.md — a short how-to focused on tool typing, local index stubs, and structured-output assertions. 4) A minimal e2e script (node) that exercises the playbook with canned embeddings and validates the linter rules.

Design notes: - Typed tool bindings: both examples include a generated ToolBinding interface that enforces input/output types for tool calls; Kotlin uses kotlinx.serialization and a small codegen stub; Swift uses Codable and a template to deserialize tool responses. - Structured-output linter: the linter is intentionally tiny (200 LOC) and validates fields, enums and simple length/format constraints against prompt-output produced JSON; it's meant to be used in CI to catch regression of contract drift. - Telemetry probes: the probes are non-blocking; they batch 1s/32 events and emit a compact event envelope (service, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, sample_rate). The quickstart shows how to hook probes into Redwood SDK request lifecycle.

Testing: Added smoke tests that run locally (no network to Redwood required) using stubbed model responses. There is one integration-only script (scripts/run-integration.sh) that is gated behind an env var QUICKSTART_INTEGRATION=true. CI runs the unit/smoke matrix by default.

Migration/compatibility: This is additive content under quickstarts; no runtime code in the core redwood SDKs was modified. The docs cross-link existing RAG authoring playbooks and telemetry docs.

Related linear items: ENG-3210 (mobile rag quickstarts), PM-412 (docs brief and acceptance criteria).

How to try locally: see quickstarts/kotlin-swift-typed-rag/README.md for step-by-step.
commits: 4d5e6f7: add structured-output linter and schema examples
8a9b0c1: telemetry probes + probe harness and example events
2b3c4d5: CI workflow matrix for kotlin + swift smoke checks
7e8f901: docs/snippets and README polish, add integration guard
review_comments: Miguel Santos (reviewer): Nice scaffold — can we make the linter schema examples cover an enum mismatch case?
Asha Patel (author): Good call — added enum sample and updated schema.json with 'response_type' enum and a unit test in scripts/test-linter.sh
Emma Chen (reviewer): CI matrix looks fine, but macOS runner increases minutes; can we gate the full Swift compile check to PRs labeled 'macos-build' to save minutes?
Asha Patel (author): Switched to a conditional step; default matrix runs macOS-lint only on tagged releases or when label applied (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md for quickstarts).
Liam O'Rourke (approver): Approved after schema + CI gating changes.
release_notes: Introduces a cross-platform (Kotlin + Swift) typed RAG quickstart demonstrating tool typing, structured-output linter, and compact telemetry probes for mobile-first scenarios. Non-breaking, experimental quickstart content intended for developer adoption and feedback.
notes_for_reviewer: Focus review on linter schema clarity and the telemetry probe event shape. The kotlin codegen is intentionally minimal and explained in the README; if you'd like I can follow-up with a generator that emits ToolBinding classes from the schema.
